en: The Great Uṣṇīṣa Tathāgata’s Radiance of the Great Divine Power of Sitātapatrā,
the Dhāraṇī Sovereign that Collects All Mantras,
Chapter One: The Great Majestic and Most Victorious Golden Wheel Samādhi Mantra.

Also titled: *The Dharma of the Independent Practice of the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa: Fearlessness*, Chapter One: "The Dhāraṇī of the Samādhi of the Most Victorious Golden Wheel of Great Majestic Virtue. Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
He was accompanied by five thousand great arhats,
including Mahākāśyapa and Uruvilvākāśyapa.
Gayākāśyapa, Nadīkāśyapa, and Śāriputra.
Mahāmaudgalyāyana,
Nanda, and Anuruddha.
Kapphiṇa, Ājñātakauṇḍinya,
and Ānanda.
Rāhula and others were the leaders;
there was also an assembly of immeasurable great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
including Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
and Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva.
Maitreya Bodhisattva and Vajragarbha Bodhisattva were the leaders.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable mantra-deities:
the deity King Vajrapāṇi,
the deity Hayagrīva, and others.
He was the foremost among them.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable vajras,
such as the Vajra-vaśirāṭa-hāsa-vajra.
He served as their leader.
Furthermore, there was the Sun Deva King,
and there were immeasurable yakṣa kings.
Āṭavaka was the leader,
and there were also the Sun Deity and the Moon Deity.
The Four Great Heavenly Kings,
the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven,
Śakra Devānām Indra.
Mahādeva, Mahābrahmā, and Tuṣita Heaven.
The Śuddhāvāsa devas, the Maheśvara devas,
and the goddess Guṇakāraṇḍavyūhā.
The Viśvakarman devas,
together with their retinues, as well as the devas and nāgas.
Ghosts and spirits, asuras, and garuḍas.
Gandharvas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
Kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, and so forth,
as well as immeasurable kings of humans and devas.
O Dragon Kings, Rākṣasa Kings,
and Bhikṣus!
Bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and so forth.
An immeasurable multitude of śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, humans, and devas, numbering as many as the sands of the Ganges, all together.
The eight classes of dragon deities surrounded him from front and back,
making offerings and paying him reverent homage.
He paid homage and offered praise,
scattering various flowers and incense over the Buddha.
Each was filled with joy;
they joined their palms in reverence,
prostrated at the Buddha's feet, and circumambulated him three times.
They sat down to one side and gazed up at the Tathāgata,
their eyes never for a moment turning away.
I wish to hear the most supreme Dharma.
At that time, within the city of Rājagṛha,
the six heretical teachers constantly practiced false views.
First, Pūraṇa Kāśyapa;
second, Mahā-Moggallāna Koṭṭhita;
third, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhiputta.
The fourth was Ajita Keśakambala;
the fifth was Kakuda Kātyāyana;
the sixth was Nirgrantha Jñātiputra.
These six great non-Buddhist teachers,
together with their retinues,
came to where the Buddha was.
Desiring to engage in a formal debate with the Tathāgata,
there was at that time a withered tree in that garden named Amla.
At that time, Pūraṇa Kāśyapa asked the Buddha, saying:
"Gautama, you are not omniscient.
If you were truly possessed of all-knowledge..."
"How is it? Is this Āmra tree truly dead, or will it live again?
At that time, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, remained silent and did not answer.
At that time, Pūraṇa Kāśyapa saw that the Buddha did not answer;
he took up a white whisk and sprinkled water upon the tree,
whereupon it immediately sprouted flowers and leaves once more.
The *puspa* flowers were in full bloom;
in a mere moment, they bore ripe fruit.
Pūraṇa Kāśyapa then ordered his disciples to pluck the fruit.
When he was about to bestow [this] upon the great assembly, at that time,
all the ordinary beings within the gathering conceived doubts and perplexity in their minds.
They marveled at this great and extraordinary anomaly—
that the Buddha did not answer but remained silent—
and concluded that, in truth, the Tathāgata does not possess omniscience.
They do not equal those of the non-Buddhists.
At that time, the World-Honored One,
knowing that doubt had arisen in the minds of the assembled multitude, [addressed them].
He immediately entered the Fire-Light Samādhi and emitted a great radiance from the crown of his head,
which illuminated the trichiliocosm.
The Buddha himself formed the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā to summon and invite the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions into the midst of space.
Buddhas and bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of immeasurable Ganges Rivers gathered from all directions like a vast cloud;
those Buddhas of the ten directions likewise emitted radiance,
with water and fire issuing forth from their bodies.
Manifesting great majestic power,
he caused those withered trees to immediately become ripe and rotten once again.
They were broken and withered;
those outside the Way and others were distressed and agitated,
clutching one another's hands.
They wailed and wept,
scattering in all directions as they fled.
At that time, the various devas remained suspended in the air.
They scattered flowers as an offering and praised the Buddha’s spiritual power with various kinds of music.
Possessing all-encompassing wisdom,
he subdued the non-Buddhists,
and the fourfold assembly rejoiced.
All of them resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, Ānanda surveyed the entire assembly and observed what was in their minds.
Thereupon, within the assembly,
he rose with composed dignity and bared his right shoulder.
With palms joined toward the Buddha,
he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and spoke these words:
Excellent!
How extraordinary! O Greatly Powerful One, Honored Teacher of Gods and Humans, what a marvelous occasion this is today!
Subduing the non-Buddhists,
he causes all sentient beings to take refuge in the True Dharma.
World-Honored One,
we śrāvakas are truly deluded and ignorant.
They delight in much learning,
yet regarding their minds subject to outflows,
they do not seek liberation.
Having received the Buddha’s compassionate instruction,
I have been able to correctly and earnestly cultivate my body and mind;
yet, though I have heard this, I am unable to achieve inner stability and peace.
Now I wish to collect my mind;
how should I subdue it?
I only pray that the World-Honored One will [instruct me].
Please explain this extensively for me,
so that I may attain non-retrogression and cause all sentient beings to do likewise.
The essential points of the Dharma were heard everywhere.
At that time, the World-Honored One,
by the power of his perfect and universal knowledge, [taught].
He praised Ānanda, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
You are able to act for the sake of the great assembly of all humans and devas."
He then asked the Tathāgata about the matter of gathering the mind.
"Listen attentively and receive this well;
reflect upon it thoroughly."
I shall first explain for you the entry into samādhi for those who practice and study.
Seeking all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvajñatā*),
one first maintains the fourfold restraint with clarity and purity.
Thus, the Tathāgata’s frost cannot give rise to any branches or leaves of the mind.
The three periods and four modes of birth are like the immeasurable causes and conditions;
thereafter, Ānanda, one should understand the Dharma of the twelve links of dependent origination.
Regarding these four matters and the twelve links of dependent origination,
if one does not harbor a lingering mind toward them and does not crave forms,
sounds, smells, tastes, or tactile objects.
"How do all demonic activities arise?
Ānanda, if there is a person who practices and studies..."
If there are those who cannot extinguish the karmic obstacles and transgressions resulting from past habitual tendencies and conditions,
you should instruct these people to repent with single-minded devotion.
To eradicate the karmic obstructions of previous lives,
one should prostrate with utmost sincerity before the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, and nāgas.
I entreat all Buddhas of the ten directions to grant their compassionate protection. With humility,
reverence, benevolence, and forbearance,
I make this vow of dedication.
Exhorting all Buddhas to remain long in the world and turn the great wheel of Dharma.
Delivering the multitudes of humans and devas,
their minds are free from distraction,
being single-mindedly focused.
One practices the method of samādhi,
exerting oneself with diligence day and night,
with a mind free from weariness or abandonment.
Seeking the supreme fruit of the pure Great Nirvana,
she was formerly a courtesan; yet,
due to the power of meditative concentration, she had no desire for sensual practice.
His heart of affection was forever liberated.
Thereupon, Ānanda felt compassion for all sentient beings.
They turn back those in the six realms of existence who are submerged in the ocean of suffering and are unable to awaken.
To provide a basis for his mind,
he addressed the Buddha again, saying,
"World-Honored One."
Having received the unsurpassed compassionate instruction of the Tathāgata,
my mind has already attained awakening;
today I shall cultivate and realize the path of no-more-learning (*aśaikṣamārga*).
One should simply keep in mind that in the age of the Final Dharma,
those who have newly begun their practice shall establish a site for the Way (a *dharmodāna*).
By relying on which teachings does one attain liberation?
How can the establishment of a boundary subdue all māras?
May all devas, nāgas, ghosts,
and spirits provide protection;
now, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, [is present].
Regarding the rules of purification,
Ānanda then asked in verse:
The Buddhas are inconceivable, and the Dharma they teach is likewise;
those who can faithfully accept and uphold it will have merit constantly following them.
May the Sugata always proclaim this to the multitudes of humans and devas for their peace and happiness.
We vow to cultivate our practice; how should it be established?
Now, for the Buddhas, devas, nāgas, and spirits, what are the pure rules?
How may we perform repentance so as to destroy and eliminate karmic obstructions?
How does one make offerings to the noble sages who have descended?
How does one take refuge and obtain the compassionate protection of the Buddhas?
How does one give rise to the great vow, issue invitations, and perform the dedication of merit?
How should one teach sentient beings so that both self and others may benefit?
We pray only that you, with great compassion,
take pity on all and extensively explain for us the essential method for receiving and upholding [the teachings].
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If there are people in future generations who wish to establish a place of practice (bodhimaṇḍa),..."
First, there was a great white ox from the Snowy Mountains,
which fed on the fatty, fragrant herbs of those mountains;
this ox drank only the fragrant, pure water of the Snowy Mountains.
That dung is so fine it can be gathered;
mixed with sandalwood, it is used as plaster.
Whether on that mountain or elsewhere, even if it is not the Snowy Mountains (Himavat), [it is the same].
The cow dung was foul-smelling and impure;
it was unfit for smearing on the ground,
so they set it aside in a level plain.
Dig through the topsoil to a depth of five chi or more,
and take the yellow earth from beneath.
The preceptor [offers] sandalwood, aloeswood,
and storax.
Frankincense, saffron,
and bdellium.
Cinnamomum tamala,
Angelica sinensis,
and Spikenard.
And *kakkola* incense.
With these ten kinds of exquisite incenses,
he ground them into a fine powder.
Mix the earth to form mud and smear it upon the site of the ritual arena,
making it sixteen feet square in circumference.
Construct an octagonal altar.
At the center of the altar, place a lotus flower made of gold, silver, copper, or wood.
In the center of the lotus flower, set a bowl.
First, fill the alms bowl with dew collected during the eighth month.
Then, take eight items—grass, wood, flowers, or leaves—from wherever they may be found within that water.
Finally, prepare a bright, pure, and perfectly clear mirror.
Each is situated within its respective enclosure.
Surrounding the flower-bowl mirror, sixteen lotus flowers are established;
sixteen incense burners are interspersed among the flowers, arranged and adorned as incense burners.
Burn only pure aloeswood incense;
do not allow the fire to be seen.
Take white cow's milk.
He set out sixteen vessels:
milk for pancakes and *śa-ya* oil cakes,
as well as milk gruel.
Suhé (styrax),
honeyed ginger,
and honeyed lotus root.
Honey and ghee;
pure ghee;
pure honey, as well as various fruits, foods, and drinks.
Grapes, rock honey,
and various other kinds of exquisite and superior foods.
Outside each lotus,
sixteen [offerings] surround the flower;
these are presented to the Buddhas and the great Bodhisattvas.
Whenever it is time for a meal,
or if it is the middle watch of the night,
take half a sheng of honey.
Use three *sruva*-ladles of clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
In front of the altar,
separately install a small fire-pit.
Boil *turuṣka* incense to produce scented water for bathing; then,
kindle the charcoal until it blazes fiercely.
Cast this ghee and honey into the charcoal brazier and burn them until the smoke has completely vanished,
then offer it to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Have banners and canopies suspended everywhere on the four outer sides.
Within the ritual chamber,
hang images of all the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions upon the four walls.
One should place Vairocana and Śākyamuni facing forward.
Maitreya, Akṣobhya,
and Amitābha.
Various great transformation images of Avalokiteśvara,
with Vajragarbha placed at their left and right,
[and] Śakra.
Brahmā-rāja,
Ucchuṣma, and Nīlambavā.
Kundali, together with the Four Heavenly Kings and the great generals of the twenty-eight classes of spirits and deities.
Together with all the devas,
nāgas, asura kings,
and Agnīśikhara Vajrapāṇi.
The Piṇāyakas are stationed at the sides of the four gates;
furthermore, eight bright mirrors are taken and placed on the left and right.
It is suspended upside down in the void,
with mirrors placed at the four corners corresponding to those installed within the ritual mandala.
By means of this correspondence, their forms and shadows will interpenetrate one another in layers;
during the first seven days,
perform prostrations with utmost sincerity.
The Tathāgatas of the ten directions,
the great Bodhisattvas,
and the Arhats.
Reciting the name,
they shall resolve to attain bodhicitta,
constantly throughout the six periods of the day and night.
Recite the mantras and circumambulate the altar;
practice the Way with a sincere mind,
doing so constantly at all times.
Recite one hundred and eight times.
During the second seven-day period,
maintain single-minded concentration.
I have made the vow for bodhicitta;
my mind is uninterrupted,
and this is my vinaya.
First, there is the teaching on the vow.
During the third seven-day period,
throughout the twelve hours.
Constantly reciting the Buddha’s *Bhadrakarātrī* mantra,
until the fourth seven-day period.
The Tathāgatas of the ten directions appeared simultaneously;
in the place where their mirrors reflected one another’s light,
they received the Buddhas’ stroking of their heads.
Thereupon, at the site of enlightenment,
he cultivated samādhi,
being able to bring about such [a state].
Those who practice and study in the final age will have bodies and minds as clear and pure as lapis lazuli.
Ānanda, if this bhikṣu’s original preceptor and the bhikṣus from the ten directions within the same assembly...
If among them there is even one who is impure,
such a site of enlightenment will for the most part not be successful.
After twenty-one days had passed,
he sat upright in meditative seclusion for one hundred days in purity.
There were those of sharp faculties who,
without rising from their seats,
attained the fruit of Srotāpanna.
Although his body and mind remain unrestrained and the holy fruit is not yet fixed,
he knows with certainty that his attainment of Buddhahood will not be in error.
As for what you ask regarding the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*),
it is established in this manner.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions...
Each caused the bodhisattvas to offer great divine mantras;
all the vajras manifested spiritual transformations and recited the mantras as offerings.
Even unto devas, nāgas,
ghosts, spirits,
and yakṣas.
The great generals and all the rishis manifested their supernatural transformations.
They recited their mantras and offered them up, each saying,
"My mantra possesses great power."
Able to subdue poisonous evils,
such multitudes as these—
immeasurable, boundless, and innumerable— all gathered together like clouds.
They all spoke these words:
"World-Honored One,
we now wish to proclaim such a divine mantra."
"I only pray that you will grant me your permission.
At that time, the World-Honored One accepted [the request] by remaining silent.
At that time, there were bodhisattvas,
devas, nāgas, spirits,
and seers possessing the five supernatural powers.
Each, before the Buddha,
expounded the causes and conditions for the divine spells they had obtained in previous lives.
As they were reciting these spells:
Each manifested the form of their respective mantra-deities,
filling the entirety of space so that not a single void remained.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from the midst of the assembly with serene composure.
He bared his right shoulder,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
and addressed the World-Honored One.
In a past life, I received dhāraṇīs from the presence of various Buddhas.
"I now wish to speak;
I pray that you will grant me your permission.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent!
You, with great compassion, wish to proclaim this divine mantra;
now is precisely the right time.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva manifested in the form of a Hayagrīva Rākṣasa and spoke this great divine mantra.
His name was Nāgeśvara;
he emitted a great radiance that eclipsed all the mantra-deities who had come.
All shall be subdued;
only one body remains manifest,
standing alone and toweringly solitary.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:

"I possess a Buddha-mantra named 'The Supreme Vajra Great Maṇḍala Dhāraṇī of the Uṣṇīṣa Tathāgata Emitting Light, the Mahā-sitātapatra, the Sovereign King of All Mantras, the Most Victorious Golden Wheel. "
With the utmost reverence,
for the benefit of all sentient beings,
there is nothing superior to this.
"This has been transmitted only from Buddha to Buddha.
You all should receive and uphold it with a single mind, conceiving a sense of its rarity. At that time, Ānanda—
In the midst of the great assembly,
he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and addressed the Buddha, saying:
Since my renunciation of the household life,
I have relied on the Buddha with arrogance and indulgence;
because I craved extensive learning, I have not yet attained realization.
Wuwei encountered that Brahmā Heaven and was deluded by its evil arts;
he has now received the secret assistance of the Tathāgata’s divine incantations.
By its power, they shall be delivered from suffering and hardship.
We only pray that the World-Honored One will look with compassion upon all beings.
He extensively proclaimed it for their sake,
out of compassion for this assembly,
as he spoke these various mantras.
And those who are currently transmigrating in future worlds,
upon hearing this divine mantra of the Buddha,
shall obtain great peace and happiness.
At that time, the great earth suddenly shook;
rivers and streams surged and boiled,
and the sun lost its brilliant radiance.
In the void above,
the heavens rained down flowers of the seven treasures,
falling in profusion and swirling in all directions.
Celestial fragrant flowers completely covered the great earth,
and celestial drums resounded of their own accord.
All the devas [perform] music,
song, and chanting.
Praising them,
they pervaded the entirety of space as fragrant breezes arose from all directions.
All the celestial seers gathered like clouds and came together,
circumambulating the Buddha hundreds of thousands of millions of times.
He prostrated at the Buddha's feet,
withdrew to stand to one side,
and with palms joined, rejoiced.
Giving rise to a sense of rare wonder,
they marveled at what had never occurred before,
gazing up with reverence at the Honored One’s countenance.
Without averting his gaze for even a moment,
at that time the Buddhas of the ten directions each commanded a great Bodhisattva.
Holding various flowers and incense,
jeweled banners, flags, and canopies,
each accompanied by retinues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
They also held incense and flowers.
The Buddhas of the ten directions addressed the great bodhisattvas, saying:
"You all hold this incense and these flowers."
While making offerings to Śākyamuni Tathāgata in the Sahā world,
they shall transmit my instructions and inquire after his well-being.
The bodhisattvas, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic authority,
came to the Sahā world and arrived at the great city of Rājagṛha within the midst of the assembly.
He circumambulated the Buddha three times,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
and withdrew to stand to one side.
They scattered various fragrant flowers into the void,
speaking these words:
Those World-Honored Ones have commanded me to come here to inquire after the World-Honored One’s health,
whether you are free from minor ailments and few afflictions.
Your daily activities are light and at ease.
You wish to expound the Great Dharma;
now is precisely the right time.
"We only pray that the World-Honored One will explain this for us and for all sentient beings.

All the śrāvakas,
bodhisattvas,
and the great assembly of humans and devas.

speaking with one voice in unison.

"World-Honored One, I pray that you will have compassion for me and explain this for my sake."
"We wish to hear it,
O Tathāgata— the secret mantra of the King of Supreme Sovereign Power who emits light.

he immediately entered samādhi,
remaining silent and still.
From within the uṣṇīṣa,
ten streams of light composed of a hundred jewels surged forth;
from within that light, [ten thousand...]
Furthermore, thousand-petaled lotus flowers surged forth from the earth;
upon their pedestals sat emanated Tathāgatas,
seated in the full-lotus posture.
From within the lotus pedestal,
atop the head of that transformation Buddha,
ten rays of light composed of a hundred jewels were again emitted.
It universally illumines the worlds of the ten directions;
from every single pore,
it emits fragrant winds.
There was a great golden wheel in the midst of space;
within its revolving radiance,
there were manifested everywhere immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of great divine kings and powerful heroes of the Vajrapāṇi Guhyakas.
Lifting up mountains and wielding a mace,
he turns the celestial wheel of the sun and manifests great supernatural powers.
Their armor gleams brilliantly;
they brandish weapons such as swords,
iron clubs, wheels, and nooses.
Bows, arrows, fishing poles, and oars;
weapons of war, bells, and chimes;
conch shells, and banners and insignia.
Banners, streamers, victory banners,
and canopies filled the entirety of space;
in some places there were thunder and lightning.
The earth shook with a great sound;
the sun and moon lost their light;
and all the devas and nāgas [were struck with awe].
They did not rest content in their own dwellings,
but all came together from their palaces like gathering clouds;
all fierce beasts ceased their breathing and laid aside their venomous hearts.
In this great assembly gathered from all quarters,
the spirits and deities, like those bearing battle banners,
comfort one another.
The great assembly looked up in awe;
filled with both fear and joy,
they each sought his compassionate protection.
At that time, within the light of the emanated Buddha’s mark of the invisible crown of the head, there appeared—
He utters the great Brahma-voice and proclaims thus,
taking refuge in and awakening the multitude of deluded beings.
Then he spoke in verse:
Homage to all Buddhas of the three periods of time! Homage to all Bodhisattvas!
Homage to the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and others! Homage to all spirits and deities!
Each of you listen clearly to my instructions: I shall now proclaim the great divine mantra;
all who hear it should rejoice. Paying homage with reverence, listen with a sincere heart.
The Buddha’s seals total thirty-two.

The Heart Mantra of the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī, also known as the Heart Mantra of All Buddhas:
Oṃ (1) sarvatathāgatamanyite (2) pravaradite jñānapraye (3) oṃ (4) śamayaṃtu mama amukaśarmaṇaḥ sarvabādhāḥ (5) svasti bhavatu.
1. Padu, 2. mumuci mumuci, 3. vimuci vimuci, 4.
carī carīṇi, 5. gati, 6. bhayakīlāṇe, 7.
padupadide, 8. padapadaye, 9. bhadri bhadri, 10. buddha-rin.
*Sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya* (16) *śūṣma* (17) *svāhā*.
For the Great Cūdāmaṇi Great Heart Mantra Seal, one should always perform it with the two middle fingers.
Place the ring fingers behind the palms,
press the two thumbs against each other,
and interlock the index fingers.
The two middle fingers are placed behind the two ring fingers;
the index fingers touch each other at their tips,
and the two ring fingers are extended upward.
Binding the two little fingers and extending the middle fingers upward constitutes the Seal of the Inconceivable Great Uṣṇīṣa for Destroying All Dharmas,
also known as the Vajra-Awful Mudrā; it is identical to the Seal of the Lesser Uṣṇīṣa for Destroying All Dharmas.
Furthermore, the Great-Head Vajra (*Mahāmūrdha-vajra*) destroys all mudrās; likewise, with the right hand,
form the right middle finger into a hook,
bending it to press against the lower part of the thumb.
Bind the thumbs and middle fingers together and extend them straight upward;
the index, ring, and little fingers of both hands are to be pointed upward.
This is the Seal of the Great Buddha-Crown for Subduing All Supernatural Powers and the Dharma of Fearlessness, formed with the two middle and ring fingers.
Interlace the ring fingers and little fingers within the palms;
bend both thumbs and insert them into the palms.
Press the two index fingers together with the left over the right;
extend the remaining fingers and interlace them.
For the three mudrās above, use the aforementioned mantra.
The Mantra and Seal of the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the Heart-Mantra of All Buddhas, and the Mantra and Seal of All Bodhisattvas. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajratī vajra pratisarati stuti tathāgatamudrādhiṣṭhāna-dhiṣṭhitā svāhā. For the Great Uṣṇīṣa Great Wrathful Seal: extend both thumbs straight upward.
The two middle fingers extend straight upward with their tips touching.
The two index fingers are slightly curved, their tips leaning against the side of the upper joint of the middle fingers.
Interlace the two ring fingers and little fingers with their tips pointing outward;
this is the seal for binding the great-sword-bearing ghosts of the Great Buddha-Crown (Mahā-ūrṇā). For the seal of the Great Buddha-Crown, extend the two thumbs straight upward.
Bend the tip of the left index finger;
with the left thumb outside the fingers,
slightly curve the tips of the right index finger and the two middle fingers beneath them.
Bend all three fingers together within the palms.

This is the Great Uṣṇīṣa Consecration Dhāraṇī, also known as the Great Uṣṇīṣa Amṛta Dhāraṇī: Oṃ (1) muñe muñe vare (2) abhiṣiñca me (3) sarvatathāgata hūṃ (4) mama amukaśarmaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ (5) viṣajite (6) mahāvajre (7) kālacāraṇe (8) pracaṇḍatīrthe (9) tathāgatādhiṣṭhite (10) ṣṭhitavajre (11) svāhā. The seal of the Great Uṣṇīṣa Consecration: keep the body level with the legs joined together.
With the right hand, direct it downward toward the spleen region.
With the left hand, bend the index, ring, little, and thumb fingers together;
keep the middle finger upright, positioned at the space between the eyebrows on the forehead.
If one performs this rite with fingernails made of *śrīparṇī* wood, all root transgressions will be completely extinguished. The mantra is:
Oṃ amṛtodbhave vara vara pravaraviśodhani haṃ haṃ phaṭ phaṭ vaṃ vaṃ svāhā. This is the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Amṛta Seal.
The middle finger of the right hand is placed between the index finger and the thumb;
the index finger presses upon the upper joint of the thumb,
and the thumb presses upon the nail of the little finger.
If a person forms this mudrā and recites this mantra,
all the devas will pour nectar over the crown of this person's head; it is inconceivable.

The Dharma for the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Boundary-Sealing Mantra: Oṃ ātmatā vairocani krodha-bhūṣaṇi akaraśani haṃ haṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. For the Great Heart Mudrā of the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa: interlace the two middle fingers within the palms.
The two little fingers are held upright side by side;
the two thumbs are held upright side by side;
and each of the two index fingers presses down on the tip of its respective thumb.
This seal can encompass all mind-seals (*cittamudrā*).
Within the True Dharma, it can encompass the four types of seals that accord with the mind.
If one performs these, one will attain mastery over all dharmas without obstruction.
First, form this mudrā and recite the mantra forty-nine times;
only then should it be employed.

The Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Heart-and-Center Mantra: Oṃ (1) vajra (2) vara-vara (3) indriya (4) viśuddhe (5) haṃ haṃ (6) curu-cure (7) kāru-care (8) svāhā. If one forms this mudrā while recollecting all the Buddhas...
All Buddhas will come before that person,
and all mantra-deities will protect them;
this is the great protection of the body.
And cause all spirits and deities to be employed.
If one wishes to recite the essential mantras,
one must first recite the Buddha’s Heart-to-Heart Mantra (Buddha-hṛdaya-hṛdaya-mantra).
For the protection of the body, perform the small Buddha-uṣṇīṣa armor mudrā: interlace the ring fingers and little fingers of both hands within the "tiger's mouth," and extend the two middle fingers.
Extend both thumbs and index fingers,
each pressing against the knuckle on the back of the middle finger;
the two thumbs then pinch the inner side of the two middle fingers.
Place the large seal of the Great Armor on the upper side of the arm.
Place the seal protruding from the chest.
If you wish to construct a mandala:
Form this mudrā and recite the mantra;
as you traverse the altar and establish the boundary,
the deities will all arrive spontaneously.
If one does not perform this seal,
the great kṣetrapāla kings will destroy the person's boundary.
If the ritual procedure is not accomplished,
bind this *kavaca-mudrā* (armor seal) and recite the mantra forty-nine times.
Placing the seal upon the chest, the two shoulders, the knees, and the crown of the head,
all the hosts of Vajras shall provide protection and attend upon one.
Upon seeing this Buddha-body,
all the non-Buddhists exhausted their supernatural powers.
That which cannot be destroyed:
the placement of the feet remains as before;
one only changes the two thumbs so that they press against the joints of the middle fingers.
It is also called the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā).
If there are evil persons or predatory beasts, one should form this seal.
Recite the mantra forty-nine times;
eighty-four thousand vajras and ten billion buddhas will protect and guard the mantra-practitioner.
Furthermore, there is the single mudrā of the hundred billion Buddhas with one mind,
called the Buddha-Cakra-mudrā.
Interlace the ring fingers and the two little fingers within the palms.
The two thumbs are held together and upright.
The two middle fingers are held side by side and upright.
Each of the two index fingers presses upon the knuckle on the back of its respective middle finger.
When forming this mudrā,
ten billion Buddhas and ten billion Bodhisattvas [appear].
Ten billion vajra-holders,
the deities of the Four Heavenly Kings,
and their military hosts.
May they all come to protect and sustain me,
causing me to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
and [warding off] all evils.
If they see one who holds this seal,
they will all give rise to kindness and compliance,
and no evil thoughts will arise.
If there are perils from kings, perils from armies, or perils from blades that seek to harm one,
one should bind this mudrā and recite the mantra forty-nine times.
The evil thief binds himself;
though he asks in confusion for his heart,
he does not understand and will never attain awakening.
Because this mudrā possesses such great power,
it is the Body Mudrā of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa:
cross the two ring fingers of the left and right hands behind the back.
Place the two little fingers straight upward within the palms;
join the tips of the two middle fingers together;
and bend the tips of the two index fingers.
Press the back of the upper phalanx of the middle fingers together,
and with the two thumbs held upright, pinch the sides of the middle phalanges of the middle fingers;
then move the index fingers back and forth.
Then he spoke the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya-mantra, saying:

*Namo sarvajñāya | Oṃ | Tathāgatoṣṇīṣa | Anavalokitamūrdhni | Mudite | Tiṣṭha rāśe | Hūṃ śatara śatara | Dhaka dhaka vidhaka vidhaka | Tara tara vidhara vidhara | Cinda cinda binda binda | Binda binda | Hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.* The mantra for destroying Māra and subduing [obstacles] follows the same body-mudrā as before.
Only change the two index fingers so that their tips are joined;
then, with the backs of the upper joints of the two middle fingers, each [middle finger] should press against the side of the [corresponding] index finger's tip.
Then, bend both thumbs and place them inside the palms;
first, one should hold it upon the crown of the head.
With a sincere heart, pay respectful homage.
With a sincere heart, recite the mantra:
Oṃ śrīye svāhā. This is the seal for the invocation.
Following the previous body mudrā,
change the two index fingers so that they stand upright,
four and a half inches apart.
Holding both thumbs upright and extending them eight *fen* from the middle fingers,
recite the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya mantra.
This is the fourth essential point:
gradually bend both index fingers into the palms.
Recite the mantra eleven times.
Then, with hand gestures (*mudrā*), bowing in prostration, they disperse inwardly.
This is the seal for the invitation (*adhyeṣaṇā-mudrā*).
Request that they perform the Flower-Light Seal (*puṣpa-prabhā-mudrā*).
The Lotus-to-Foot [Mudrā],
also known as the Flower-Radiance Seal (Puṣpaprakāśamudrā):
join the two little fingers together, pointing them upward.
With both thumbs together and the remaining six fingers spread apart and held upright,
slightly bend the finger joints in the manner of opening a flower.
Recite the mantra seven times,
bend both index fingers toward the palms,
and immediately perform prostrations facing inward.
Dissolve the Lotus Seal.
The mantra for the seat is:
Oṃ kamala-svāhā. Recite this seven times. This purification mantra is applicable across all families (kulas).
Recite this mantra over water seven times: Oṃ vajramaṇidhāri haṃ haṃ phaṭ phaṭ. This is the mantra for entering places where one has touched [impurities].
Recite it seven times each time one goes to the toilet.
Snap the fingers three times.
Oṃ kuruḍana hūṃ śve. When eating, recite this mantra seven times.
And to expel the vināyakas:
Oṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the mantra for purifying the mouth. First, before every recitation, [recite]: Oṃ sādhidevatā nārāyaṇāya ṭhaḥ svāhā.
Wash [the hands] and recite seven times.
The mantra for purifying the body is:
Oṃ vajramaṇidhāri hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. With this, pass through impure places.
Recite this seven times;
it will be as if one has bathed in fragrant water, and furthermore,
it will extinguish the defilement of transgressions.

Regarding the mudrā and mantra for protecting the body from the *Cintāmaṇicakra* rite: interlace the two index fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers within the palms, with the right hand placed over the left.
Bend the heads of the two middle fingers and press them against the backs of the two index fingers so that they touch.
Extend both thumbs together and press them against the sides of the middle fingernails.
The mantra is:
Oṃ Krodhana Hūṃ Cchaḥ. Recite this while forming this mudrā.
Recite this mantra three times to protect yourself when going to various places where contact occurs, as well as when going to the toilet;
do so whenever you arrive at such a location.
Holding earth to cleanse the hands,
as well as rinsing the mouth and teeth,
[one uses] the right hand’s thumb, index finger, and middle finger.
Slightly bend the ring fingers and hook the little fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ ture hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. Form this mudrā and receive the consecrated water seven times;
rinse the mouth and clean the teeth.
Furthermore, while drinking and sprinkling water to exorcise all *vajra* spirits and demons,
one should clasp both hands together with the backs touching and visualize oneself in a state of wrathful anger.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Having done so, quickly turn both hands over and join the palms together properly.
Recite it seven more times,
then immediately use both hands to swiftly pry it open.
The mantra of the Four Heavenly Kings is as follows:

Namo ratnatrayāya (1). Namo jatur-mahājaya (2). Vivicchutaṅ (3). Mahājaya (4). Vairocana-mahājaya (5). Dharī-aśitur (6). Sthāye sthāye hṛdi dhandha hṛdi dhandha buddhabhate (7). Bodhisattvasaye (8). Prati-ka (9). Buddhasvabhate sūryabhate (10). Candra-bhate (11). He he ti (12). Chachiti (13). Hu hu mahābhate (14). He he mahābhate (15). Svāhā vajramukhiṃ paṇḍani svāhā (16). This is the seal-formula for the *Koṭi-sūtra* used for the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandhana*).
Interlace the two middle fingers and the two ring fingers of both hands so that they enter the palms,
with the right hand pressing over the left.
Bend the left index finger into a hook shape.
With the right index finger held straight up and the two thumbs joined face-to-face,
one forms the following sublime mantra:
Recite "Oṃ jñānīkīlaya svāhā" once.
With the thumb of the mudrā,
touch the ground once.
Like the movement of a blade of grass, perform the mudrā three times.
Form the fire-court seal of the external fire boundary; for this seal, cover it closely with the left hand.
Place the backs of the right hands together and hold them upright;
with the two thumbs separated by about two inches, one forms the mudrā of the Wondrous Speech. It is said:
Recite "Oṃ asamañji hūṃ svāhā" three times.
Perform the mudrā by circling it to the right three times. This is it.
Oṃ jitāri jita. Furthermore, if one suffers from leprosy, malignant sores,
or bodily pain, one should empower water with this mantra seven times.
By bathing the body, one attains recovery.
Furthermore, if there are centipedes,
snakes, or scorpions...
Dragons, beasts,
tigers, wolves, and lions.
If horses, pigs, dogs, or other animals bite [a person],
one should recite the mantra over water once and wash the affected area;
the affliction will immediately be extinguished.
Furthermore, there is a dharma:
if one has fallen ill due to talismans, incantations, curses, or the use of *gū* (poisonous charms),
one should recite a mantra over seven grains of mustard seed.
Strike the sick person;
as soon as you strike, you will know for yourself the point of aversion.
Then recite the mantra once more.
By pouring [the water] upon the crown of his head,
he was cured. Furthermore,
there was another person who was ill.
This is caused by spirits;
you should command the Four Heavenly Kings to protect the patient.
Recite the mantra once over a branch of a pomegranate tree and strike it into the air.
Then, have the patient state their own name.
Furthermore, if there is a disease of sores that breaks out every day or every other day:
For those who fall ill on the third day,
take one handful of consecrated ashes and use them to encircle the patient.
It shall be removed immediately.
Furthermore, if there are any dharmas that do not achieve their intended effect,
it is entirely because karmic obstructions reside within one's person.
Take flowing water from the east and recite the mantra over it seven times;
then pour it upon the head of the mantra-reciter,
and immediate divine efficacy will be attained.
This causes the spirit of the mantra to take up residence in their hearts.
Furthermore, if there are any obstacles or difficulties within the body of the mantra-practitioner, [the following shall be done].
Take one part of ox bezoar and recite the mantra over it seven times.
If it is applied to the hairline, one will attain freedom from obstacles.
Furthermore, if there is one who has been harmed by poisonous medicine,
one should recite the mantra once over indigo juice or "well-flower" water (the first bloom of a well).
Administer it as a nasal drop,
and he will immediately recover.
Furthermore, take one *sheng* of "well-flower" water and recite [the mantra] over it seven times.
When the sun first rises,
one should face it and consume it oneself;
all illnesses will be completely healed.
Sprinkle the remaining water toward the sun.
May all sentient beings in the world be freed from every illness and obstacle.
All shall be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, recite the mantra once over water and a single grain of white mustard seed.
Recite the mantra once and scatter water within the house;
recite the mantra over seven grains of white mustard seed.
Bury it within the house;
no ghosts or spirits whatsoever shall enter.
Furthermore, there is another method.
Chant the mantra over water once and use it for consecration and washing the face;
all disputes and legal troubles will be extinguished.
People who see it rejoice.
Furthermore, there is a dharma:
if one travels across the great ocean, rivers, mountains, streams, or wildernesses;
Recite the mantra over water once;
by departing [with this water], one will immediately be free from fear.
Furthermore, if one is in a mountain valley, a forest, or a secluded place, [the same applies].
Burn incense, scatter flowers,
and recite mantras. All Buddhas.
Bodhisattvas,
devas, nāgas,
and spirits.
They all appeared before him in person and preached the sublime Dharma to him,
even bestowing upon him the elixir of the immortals.
Furthermore, if one suffers from shi-feng (epidemic wind),
headaches,
or heat and pain in the face and eyes;
Recite the mantra over ghee, curd, and honey once;
by applying it, one will be healed immediately.
Furthermore, if there should be an evil person...
If one wishes to come and cause harm,
one should recite the mantra three times with a sincere mind before sunrise.
All malicious people with wicked tongues will naturally be extinguished.
Furthermore, there is a dharma.
If one desires to seek the wealth and property of others,
by reciting the mantra seven times, one shall obtain them both when going and returning.
Furthermore, within a pure chamber:
As incense was burned and mantras were recited,
all the celestial maidens manifested their forms and performed divine music.
One should make offerings to the mantra-reciter,
or seek them from him;
then all food and drink from the heavens will be available according to one's wishes.
Furthermore, if there are people who harbor mutual hatred and jealousy,
one should recite the mantra over water once and sprinkle it upon their two doorways;
they will both immediately experience joy.
Furthermore, if one is engaged in buying, selling, or bartering in the marketplace,
one should recite the mantra over a peacock feather once and carry it with one.
One will obtain great benefit.
Furthermore, if a person dies suddenly and three days have passed, [one should perform the following].
Recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Then, recite it over a branch of a pomegranate tree;
strike the crown of the head seven times and the person will revive.
Furthermore, if there is someone who has died suddenly,
having been struck by a ghost,
one should recite the mantra over water once.
Sprinkle it upon his face,
and he will immediately recover.
Furthermore, if [this occurs] within a stūpa...
Alternatively, within a clean room,
take pure earth and blend it with sandalwood.
Construct a three-tiered square altar according to its required size,
and adorn it with various kinds of grasses and flowers.
Distribute these upon the altar.
Take a crystal flask and fill it completely with clarified butter (sarpis).
Furthermore, place seven grains of śarīra within the vase and set it upon the altar.
The person performing the ritual shall spread a clean mat and sit upon it to the west of the altar.
With a sincere heart, kneel with the right knee on the ground,
burn incense, scatter flowers,
and recite and uphold the Great Dharani.
Before it had passed through seven cycles,
at that moment, the śarīra emitted a brilliant light.
As for those who practice this illumination,
the person reciting the mantra should,
with a sincere heart, prostrate and make a vow.
Take this clarified butter (sarpis) and consume it yourself;
all obstacles and difficulties [will be eliminated].
He completely eradicated them all.
Furthermore, he took the relics,
placed them in a pouch, and wore them upon his head.
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits will never be far from them,
surrounding and protecting them as they would look upon a Buddha.
All sentient beings who see him rejoice,
and they pay him homage and make offerings to him with reverence.
Ānanda, this Dharma is inconceivable;
it is the power of merit.
May all sentient beings be free from calamities and have their karmic rewards fulfilled.
Furthermore, if all sentient beings...
Seeing a fierce beast wishing to devour him,
he recited a mantra and pointed his finger at it;
the beast immediately prostrated itself and did not rise.
Both shall attain liberation.
Furthermore, on the night of the twenty-ninth day of the dark fortnight,
one should go to a wilderness or a cemetery.
By burning incense and reciting mantras,
one will immediately cause the piśāca spirits to come and pay homage.
Or one may offer precious jewels as an offering.
If one wishes for the messenger to oversee affairs so that all matters,
both good and evil, are fully known, [one should do so].
Ānanda, I shall now explain for you the Great Seal Dhāraṇī-mother, which is capable of destroying evil karma.
Join the two index fingers, bending them into the palms.
Press the joints of the middle phalanges of the index fingers with both thumbs;
while the remaining three fingers of each hand are joined together in *añjali*, recite the mantra.
This is called the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-prabhāsa-dhāraṇī-mudrā.
Ānanda, again, with the right hand, press the nail-joint of the middle finger with the thumb,
and extend the remaining fingers;
this is called the Seal of the Tathāgata’s Well-Assembled Dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, with the right hand,
press the two little fingers and the ring fingers upon their respective nails,
and extend the remaining fingers.
This is called the Seal of the Imperial Edict.
The Tathāgata shall employ this seal to transform and guide devas, humans, asuras, and others.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"After my parinirvāṇa,
if there is someone who can recite this divine mantra seven times every day,"
One should extinguish all extremely heavy and grave offenses and obtain great virtuous vows and boundless merit. It is,
for example, like a person who...
If one practices the perfection of giving by bestowing the precious treasures of the four continents as an offering,
the merit thereof is a hundred thousand million times greater [than the former].
It is not as good as reciting and upholding [the mantra] with a sincere mind before an image of the Buddha at dawn.
If this mantra is recited seven times,
its merit and power of blessing will,
when compared to the previous merit, [surpass it].
A hundredth part does not equal it;
indeed, even calculation, analogy, or metaphor cannot reach it.
This mantra enables the one who upholds it.
May they swiftly realize the perfect site of enlightenment.
May the Tathāgatas of the ten directions...
All praise and extol you,
saying that your attainment of Buddhahood in a future age will not be in vain;
the radiance of your body shines forth brilliantly.
Ānanda, throughout all Buddha-fields,
in every place wherever they may be.
In whatever land and among whatever sentient beings this mantra exists,
the devas and nāgas will rejoice.
The winds and rains accord with the seasons;
the five grains ripen in abundance;
and the people live in peace and happiness.
It can also subdue all malevolent stars,
regional portents and anomalies,
and all calamities and obstacles.
None of these arise;
no one dies of madness;
there are no cangues, fetters, or shackles.
They do not become attached to their bodies;
they sleep throughout the night,
and never have bad dreams.
Ānanda, in this Sahā world,
there are eighty-four thousand calamitous and malevolent stars.
The twenty-eight great malevolent stars serve as the foremost,
and there are further eight great malevolent stars that act as their lords.
Manifesting in various forms throughout the world,
they are able to give birth to sentient beings.
All various calamities and anomalies that exist upon this ground where this mantra resides shall be entirely extinguished.
If one is able to uphold it,
one shall obtain great peace and security for twelve yojanas.
The ground of the boundary is thus established;
all evil portents and calamities can never enter.
For this reason, the Tathāgata has proclaimed this secret,
unsurpassed dhāraṇī mantra.
Abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi,
his qualities could not be fully described;
he serves as a great refuge for Jambudvīpa.
A treasure for the poor;
an excellent medicine for the sick;
a guide for the blind.
The great path to bodhi is free from all further obstructions;
[this applies to] all hungry ghosts.
Poor sentient beings obtain great wealth and happiness;
those imprisoned and confined [are released].
All shall attain liberation.
Ānanda, if a person’s mind is distracted,
it is not samādhi.
If one briefly recollects and upholds this mantra,
all bodhisattvas and vajras [will be present].
Śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and ṛṣis.
The eight classes of dragon deities constantly come to provide protection;
how much more so for those who are resolute!
The bodhicitta arises;
it arises in the families of yakṣas and rākṣasas who have not yet produced [the thought of awakening],
as well as in all the families of asuras.
Even unto hungry ghosts and animals;
those with form and those without form;
those with perception and those without perception.
Those with feet and those without feet—
vipers, snakes, vipers, scorpions,
and all other classes of wriggling and sentient beings.
If such evil places as these are heard but once by the ear,
one shall never again undergo them.
If this body [of the scripture] is recited,
or written out, or explained, or worn as an amulet,
or hidden away in various forms;
Making offerings throughout kalpa after kalpa,
one will never be born into poverty or low station;
wherever one is born, one will always possess the knowledge of recollecting past lives.
Possessing wealth, nobility, and mastery,
they shall in the future be born within the palaces of the devas; therefore,
it can cause those who break the precepts [to attain such results].
With the roots of their precepts purified,
those who lacked diligence naturally became diligent,
and those who lacked wisdom attained wisdom.
Those who are impure do not observe the fast and precepts.
In this way, they are all fully adorned. Good son!
Before reciting the mantra,
and after breaking the observance of the mantra,
there are the various transgressions of the precepts.
The gravity and lightness of the immediate transgressions are simultaneously extinguished,
even if one has subsequently consumed alcohol.
Consuming the five pungent roots and various kinds of impurities can cause all the Vajras,
Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas [to turn away].
Celestial immortals, spirits, ghosts,
nāga kings, and the eight classes of beings will not regard it as a transgression even if one wears impure or tattered clothing.
Whether sitting or lying down in a pure place or an impure place,
they are entirely and equally pure.
Even if one does not construct an altar,
does not enter a sacred precinct,
and does not practice the Way.
However, merely reciting the mantra is equivalent to entering the altar;
the merit of practicing the Way is no different.
This is the mantra for summoning all bodhisattvas:
Oṃ vaśyāpata svāhā. With the left and right hands joined in añjali at the heart.
Squatting with the knees apart,
bend the middle finger of the left hand to press down upon the back of the middle joint of the middle finger of the right hand.
The two thumbs point forward,
while the remaining fingers are joined together.
This is [the mudrā] if the mantra-practitioner has not yet constructed a maṇḍala.
However, whenever one forms this mudrā,
one should face the Buddha and recite the mantra seven times.
Burn incense and prostrate in worship;
then recite [the name],
which extinguishes the grave offenses of eighty kalpas.

Chapter Two: The Ten Thousand Practices of All Bodhisattvas. From the *Mahābuddhoṣṇīṣa-tathāgata-prabhā-sitātapatra*, Chapter Two: The Ten Thousand Practices of All Bodhisattvas. At that time, after the Buddha had spoken the mantra, he proceeded to explain the methods of the mudrās.
He addressed the great assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
"You gods, ghosts, and spirits,
all kneel with palms joined."
They all spoke these words:
"We now wish and delight to protect [them]."
And he spoke the mantra, saying:
"The invocation of the Seal-Mantra of the Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa is:
Oṃ īkṣe īkṣe sadaye pādāye svāhā. [He performed this] with his left and right hands.
Interlace the little fingers toward each other;
bend the two thumbs into the palms,
and extend the remaining fingers.
Recite the preceding mantra seven times.
Once the altar has been prepared,
first perform this mudrā.
Recite the aforementioned mantra every day to make offerings to the Bodhisattva,
thereby extinguishing the transgressions of broken precepts.
The mantra for invoking the Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa is as follows:
